output.subject: Your mortgage application and upcoming closing
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for calling us about your purchase mortgage application. We understand how stressful this must be with your closing date so close, and we're sorry for the worry this has caused.

You told us that your closing is scheduled for 9/14 and that you are concerned it may be missed. You mentioned that your loan officer has not returned your calls for about a week, and that underwriting has asked you for the same documents several times. You also told us that your rate lock expires on 9/16 and that you could lose your $9,800 deposit if the closing does not go ahead as planned.

You asked for your application to be processed in time for your 9/14 closing and for your loan officer to get back to you. We have shared everything you told us with our Mortgage Servicing team, who will review your concerns.

We will respond to you within 10 business days. If anything changes in the meantime, please let us know.

Kind regards,

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Closing is 9/14 and rate lock expires 9/16; the 10-business-day response window may fall after both, so decide whether faster contact is needed.
Confirm whether the loan officer or a manager has already contacted the customer since the call.
Check which documents underwriting has requested repeatedly and whether any are actually outstanding.
Decide what, if anything, to say about the rate lock and closing timeline; the draft makes no commitment.
The draft does not address the $9,800 deposit beyond acknowledging it; decide whether any further response is appropriate.
The representative's note says urgent emails went to the underwriting and loan officer managers; confirm status before sending.
